features: WHAT THE PROGRAM KNEW AND DIDN'T SAY — There is a single thread running through this release: the checks worked, they fired, they refused the operation — and what reached the administrator was a silent screen, or a wrong number on a document. No migration. From now on, though, assigning a unit to a person also registers them as a resident of that building — a link that previously was never written; it applies to new entries and changes nothing that already exists.

YOU COULDN'T COLLECT A PAYMENT IN AN IMPORTED BUILDING. You would import the building — people, units, thousandths, balances reconciled to the cent — and then you couldn't record a single payment. Measured on a building imported with beta.47: 16 people owning a unit, none of them recognised as residents. The cause was two different answers to the same question: the screen offered payers among those who own a unit, while the check on save demanded a different link that the importer never wrote. Anyone who has already imported need do nothing: existing buildings unblock themselves, without touching their data.

THE REASON FOR A REFUSAL IS NOW READABLE. Three situations in payment collection ended in an error page, throwing away the allocation you had just made by hand across dozens of instalments: credit belonging to someone unconnected to the unit, credit already spent elsewhere, insufficient credit. They now return to the filled-in form with the reason written out — «the credit you chose is no longer available: reload the page» instead of an internal code, and for insufficient credit both how much there is and how much is needed.

AND NOW THERE IS SOMEWHERE TO READ IT. That screen displayed errors only for the cash account and the date: everything else, including the checks added in the two previous releases, reached the browser and appeared nowhere at all. The button simply looked broken. There is now a band above «Confirm collection» listing every reason.

SUPPLIER PAYMENTS WERE ALSO REFUSING IN SILENCE. Payment registration handles outcomes with a list of anticipated cases, and anything not on that list vanished: the check on an inconsistent withholding tax — a fiscal figure — and more generally every ordinary check, from a missing supplier to a future date. Now everything without a window of its own is displayed, and refusals have a window distinct from technical faults: that one said «retry», and retrying unchanged achieved nothing.

THE PRINTED APPORTIONMENT NOW MATCHES WHAT WAS CHARGED. The document you take to the meeting was produced by a second engine that had fallen behind the one generating the actual charges. On a unit held in bare ownership with a usufruct, the system charged the bare owner while the printout showed zero: the row didn't add up to its own total, and the columns didn't add up to the grand total. On the same sheet.

ON EXTRAORDINARY PLANS IT WAS WORSE, ON FIVE FRONTS AT ONCE: the apportionment of a partially financed invoice was printed in full; prior-year invoices produced a blank sheet despite instalments having been issued correctly; ordinary lines on a mixed invoice inflated the document; and a cost charged to a single unit — repairing one balcony — appeared shared out among everyone. The fix was not to realign the second copy, it was to take the calculation away from it: the engine now states how much goes to each budget item. Costs charged to a single unit have a column of their own, «Direct charge», because they belong to no thousandths table.

PAYMENT COLLECTION IS EASIER TO READ. The page did not adapt to screen height: it was pinned to a height almost no laptop has, producing three nested scrollbars to show less than what was there — a large monitor saw exactly as much as a laptop. The form on the left is now always complete and scrollbar-free, and the instalment list scrolls inside its own card: on the same screen it went from two visible instalments to four, and on a large monitor it grows further. The registration preview now takes up space only when it has something to show.

A COMPLETE COLLECTION GUIDE, opened from the header, covering the screen's thirty operations and the behaviours you cannot infer from their names: «Pay all» acts only on visible rows, «Show overdue» hides rather than highlights, «Reset» leaves the page in manual mode.

Fixed — CLEARING THE NAME from the search menu left the list on the right unchanged. Searching by unit was worse: removing the unit did nothing at all, and the confirm button stayed active above the instalments of a unit no longer selected.

Under the hood: twenty-six new tests. Among them one that reads the source code and fails if a generic error type reappears in payment collection, and the first checks of agreement between the apportionment engine and its printout, which existed in no form whatsoever — which is precisely why the divergence survived. Also added the missing safety net on splitting a budget item across several thousandths tables: no test verified it to the cent.
